bullets.title: NVDA Q2 record $96B revenue, 106% YoY; Trump touts 70% FY2028 growth forecast
bullets.body: Nvidia posted Q2 revenue of $96.2B (+106% YoY), net income of $59.7B (+126% YoY), and 66% net margins at all-time highs. Q3 guidance came in at ~$108B, implying 89% YoY growth. Trump publicly congratulated Jensen Huang, calling results 'incredible.' This was NVDA's 16th consecutive quarterly revenue beat, with Wall Street consistently underestimating the trajectory. Tom Lee (Fundstrat) characterized NVDA as 'inexpensive' post-print.

bullets.title: NVDA breaks out above $218 technical level; VXN <22 supports Quad1 risk-asset run
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged $218 as the NVDA breakout level with trend support at $207 and resistance to $230, noting KOSPI front-ran the move. VXN weakened into the print, dropping below 22 and putting Nasdaq in Hedgeye's 'Investable Bucket' for Quad1 risk assets. Consensus had been buying protection pre-print, creating a clean unwind.

bullets.title: NVDA pauses revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies; antitrust concerns cited
bullets.body: Nvidia stepped back from revenue-sharing arrangements with AI cloud providers last week per WSJ, with the pause attributed to antitrust concerns over how much Nvidia may dictate customer business practices. Nvidia denied a broader pause, citing a 'new business model introduced in July' that expands compute access to fast-growing segments. One trader questioned whether rising GPU rental prices are sustainable without Nvidia subsidizing the market by renting unused capacity back from customers.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Hugging Face for $12.9B, expanding AI model platform
bullets.body: Nvidia announced an agreement to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, broadening its AI ecosystem and model hosting capabilities. Separately, NVDA filed to establish an employee-funded U.S. political action committee per Reuters.

bullets.title: NVHBM: Nvidia moves HBM controller into base die; Samsung takes early lead as supplier
bullets.body: Nvidia announced NVHBM, moving the HBM memory controller into the base die with Amazon's Annapurna as the first customer. Samsung is positioned to be the key NVHBM supplier following HBM4 development. One analyst assessed the announcement as extending Nvidia's architectural control from GPUs into memory, modestly negative for AMD.

bullets.title: MRVL Q2 FY2027 beats on revenue and EPS; Q3 guide above consensus; stock down ~8-11% AH
bullets.body: Marvell reported Q2 revenue of $2.74B (+37% YoY) vs $2.71B estimate, non-GAAP EPS $0.94 vs $0.93 est, and data center revenue of $2.172B (+46% YoY). Q3 guidance came in at ~$3.15B revenue (vs $3.03B est) and EPS of $1.05–$1.15 (midpoint $1.10 vs $1.07 consensus). Despite the beats, the stock fell 8–11% AH on margin trajectory concerns and high expectations. CEO Matt Murphy guided FY2027 revenue ~$12B (+45% YoY) with data center growing ~60%.

bullets.title: MRVL earnings read-through: CXL adoption, switch-silicon share gains vs AVGO, Photonic Fabric progress
bullets.body: Fintwit analysts flagged multiple MRVL call highlights: CXL was extensively discussed with bullish momentum expected to strengthen by year-end; Marvell's switch-silicon traction was characterized as a 'share risk to Broadcom and demand validation for Arista'; and Photonic Fabric customers are already evaluating the product lineup announced at FMS in August. One analyst noted AI infrastructure investment is broadening materially beyond accelerators into optical interconnect and Ethernet.

bullets.title: Memory shortage to last through end of 2030: SK Hynix CEO dismisses oversupply risk
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO stated the global memory chip shortage is expected to persist through the end of 2030, asserting 'memory chips are no longer commodities in the AI era.' Separately, Kioxia and SanDisk committed $31B to Kitakami NAND expansion through 2032, driven by AI demand and competitive pressure from YMTC. SK Hynix's NAND flash business continues to struggle with productivity gaps vs. Samsung.

bullets.title: MU: Trump praises $10B U.S. investment; investor expresses long-term conviction despite flat price
bullets.body: Trump publicly congratulated Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, calling MU 'one of the hottest companies in the world' and highlighting a $10B investment in new U.S. research labs. One trader expressed 'supreme long-term conviction' in MU despite near-flat price action, citing incrementally positive new data points. SK Hynix separately indicated openness to additional U.S. investment beyond its $4B Indiana HBM fab targeted for H2 2029.

bullets.title: Salesforce up 22% in single session; PLTR and software sector leadership intact
bullets.body: CRM surged over 22% in a single trading day. Hedgeye flagged PLTR as continuing to 'print' in its Signal Strength Stocks framework. The iShares Software ETF (IGV) hit year-to-date highs, up 47% from its April low. One analyst contrasted SFDC's 'deep embrace of frontier closed models' against PLTR's open-weight/customer-owned AI approach.

bullets.title: IREN FY2026 results: revenue beat, massive net loss on $450M non-cash impairments from mining hardware conversion
bullets.body: IREN reported Q4 revenue of $137.2M (vs ~$135M est) but posted a $684M net loss driven by $450M in non-cash impairments as mining hardware was decommissioned for AI conversion. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $19.2M from $59.5M in the prior quarter. AI infrastructure supply—not demand—remains the constraint per the earnings call. One analyst noted risk/reward concerns vs. CIFR ($7B vs $14.5B market cap with comparable backlogs).

bullets.title: AFRM Q4 beats: $1.166B revenue, GMV +36% YoY to $14.1B
bullets.body: Affirm reported Q4 revenue of $1.166B, beating the $1.11B estimate, with GMV growing 36% year-over-year to $14.1B.

bullets.title: Vertiv well-positioned as liquid cooling and 800V DC become baseline AI data center specs
bullets.body: One analyst flagged that liquid cooling and 800V DC are 'becoming baseline specifications' with legacy air-cooled capacity facing accelerating obsolescence. Vertiv Holdings was cited as positioned for 'positive, high-magnitude impact' from this transition. Separately, there is a 3.7-year average wait for U.S. grid connections for data centers, a structural bottleneck constraining capacity buildout.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO likely late Sept/early Oct; investor day mid-September; Pentagon ban ruled unlawful
bullets.body: Anthropic is expected to host an investor day in mid-September ahead of a likely late-September or early-October IPO, with the prospectus planned after Labor Day. The company is mulling allowing shareholders to sell in the IPO with an extended lockup. Separately, a U.S. judge ruled that the Pentagon's blacklist of Anthropic was unlawful.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole: Fed Warsh speech key event; options market may be underpricing tail risk
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh delivered his closely watched Jackson Hole keynote Friday. One analyst flagged that tail risk is 'cheaply priced' in options with CTAs stretched short in Treasuries, making the setup asymmetric. Fed officials remain divided: Collins is open to rate hikes if disinflation stalls; Schmid says rates aren't restraining the economy; Hammack says now is the time to act on price pressures.

bullets.title: Macro: German 10Y hits 15-year high; Japan 2Y auction weakest demand since 2016; JGBs falling
bullets.body: German 10-year bond yields hit their highest level in over 15 years. Japan's 2-year bond auction showed the weakest demand since 2016. JGBs are tracking declines in U.S. Treasuries, with 30-year yields at 4.085% and 40-year at 4.15%. Japan CPI remains elevated with Tokyo August CPI at +1.9% YoY in line with estimates.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: commodity traffic at 5 vessels vs 10-day avg of 15; oil flows recovering to 7-8M bpd
bullets.body: Commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to just 5 on Thursday vs a 10-day average of 15—a 67% decline from recent norms. However, total oil flows have rebounded to 7-8M bpd from ~4M bpd in mid-July, with Kuwait and Qatar restoring shipments to ~70% of pre-war levels via shuttle operations. CENTCOM confirmed sea mines have been cleared from transit routes. Brent crude settled at $89.70/bbl (+2.12%).

bullets.title: SNDK and Kioxia commit $31B to Japan NAND expansion; AI packaging demand tightening wire bonding supply
bullets.body: SanDisk and Kioxia plan over $31B in Japan investment through 2032, with a first phase including an $11.3B new fab in northern Japan to meet AI-driven demand. AI server shipment growth is simultaneously tightening supply across both advanced and traditional chip packaging, with wire bonding equipment becoming increasingly constrained according to DIGITIMES.

bullets.title: TSMC: Moody's raises outlook to positive, affirming Aa3 rating
bullets.body: Moody's affirmed TSMC's Aa3 ratings and raised the outlook to positive, signaling improved credit strength for the world's leading foundry.

bullets.title: September seasonality headwind: S&P 500 enters historically worst month; hedge fund longs at 4-year lows
bullets.body: SPY's September is the only month averaging negative total returns since 2010, per fintwit seasonality trackers. Separately, one analyst flagged that hedge fund consensus longs are down 40% since June and at 4-year lows, while the SPY drawdown from the June/July high was only 5.7%—suggesting limited prior correction. Tech positioning described as 'washed out' with $1.3T AI capex as catalyst.
